themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing Across Flushing
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 10 THIS WEEK—a 789% increase over the 8-week baseline of 1.1 per week—suggesting systematic removal, theft, or neglect that could impact navigation and traffic safety across CD 407.
evidence: 10 street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.57)
789% spike represents the sharpest deviation in the dataset
Pattern suggests concentrated incident or systemic infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Ground reconnaissance: which street signs are missing, in which neighborhoods, and what areas lack directional/regulatory signage?
DOT response: how quickly does the city repair or replace missing signs, and what is the backlog in CD 407?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Surge in Flushing
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints jumped to 7 THIS WEEK—a 522% spike over the 8-week average of 1.1 per week—indicating a potential new vandalism wave or gang activity that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.53)
Second-largest spike in the dataset, indicating acute emergence
Concentrated timing suggests coordinated activity or sudden deterioration
reporting_angles: Visual survey: map the graffiti hotspots and interview residents about perceived safety changes
NYPD/community patrol: have police noticed uptick in vandalism complaints or gang tagging in Flushing?

themes_detail.label: Underground Infrastructure Failures Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints hit 12 LAST WEEK—a 317% jump over the 8-week average of 2.9 per week—while general construction/plumbing complaints spiked 158% to 41 last week, signaling widespread subsurface deterioration.
evidence: Root/sewer/sidewalk complaints: 12 last week vs. 2.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.65, up 317%)
General construction/plumbing complaints: 41 last week vs. 15.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.12, up 158%)
Community Board has open, repeated budget request to 'Inspect water main on specific street segment and repair or replace as needed' (DEP)—suggests known, unresolved problem
Combined spike indicates coordinated failure across water/sewer systems
reporting_angles: Investigative: which street segments have the most complaints, and when was the last city inspection/repair?
Interview DEP on water main inspection schedule in Flushing; tie to recurring CB budget requests and pattern of deferred maintenance
Resident impact: document basement flooding, sidewalk collapses, or plumbing backups linked to aging infrastructure

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Spike Unexpectedly
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints jumped to 3 THIS WEEK—a 700% increase over the 8-week average of 0.4 per week—suggesting a new source of disruption or event-related activity requiring clarification.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.42, up 700%)
Timing suggests event, seasonal activity, or new recurring disturbance
Limited baseline makes spike statistically notable but context-dependent
reporting_angles: Which Flushing parks are affected, and what is the source: construction, events, youth activity, or equipment?
NYC Parks Department: are there permitted events, maintenance schedules, or new programs driving complaints?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk and Street Obstruction Wave
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints surged to 31 LAST WEEK—a 153% increase over the 8-week average of 12.2 per week—indicating growing encroachment of vending, scaffolding, or debris blocking pedestrian access across Flushing.
evidence: 31 obstruction complaints last week vs. 12.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.07, up 153%)
Coupled with street sign and graffiti spikes, suggests broader street-level infrastructure and quality-of-life degradation
Multiple active ULURP rezonings (Northern Boulevard x2, Flushing Commons RD Mod) may be attracting construction/temporary barriers
reporting_angles: Street audit: photograph and map obstructions (vending setups, construction barriers, abandoned items) in commercial districts, especially around Northern Boulevard development sites
DOB enforcement: are building permits and sidewalk shed regulations being enforced on active construction projects?
